A few things
to know.

More detail lives in the README.

What is Capture director?

Capture director is a local command-line tool that records polished website demo videos from YAML shot lists. It uses Playwright, Google Chrome, and ffmpeg to add eased zooms and a clean cursor, then assemble clips, cards, captions, and music.

Is Capture director free?

Yes. Capture director is open source under the MIT license. Download the source from GitHub and run it on your own machine. There’s no subscription or account to create.

What do I need to run it?

You’ll need macOS (the platform tested so far), Node.js 20 or newer, installed Google Chrome, and ffmpeg with libx264. It’s a command-line tool, not a packaged desktop app.

Can Codex or Claude Code use it?

Yes. The repository includes an agent skill for scouting pages, writing shot lists, recording clips, and checking contact sheets. You can also write and run the YAML yourself.

Does my recording leave my computer?

Recording and rendering run locally, with no telemetry or automatic uploads. Chrome visits the URLs in your shot list; external fonts or music in your timeline can also use the network. Every shot starts in a fresh, logged-out browser profile.

What kind of video does it export?

The defaults produce 1920 × 1080 H.264 video at 30 fps. You can change the output size, frame rate, and quality in your shot list. The render command can add crossfades, title cards, captions, and a music bed.
